```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
```
```{r}

# load in BRFSS dataset:

brfss = read.csv("brfss2022_m62.csv", stringsAsFactors=TRUE)


```



```{r}

# Running Chisq test to compare proportions between veterans and national data (gemini-gen)
# 1. Clean the data: Filter for Veterans and non-NA race entries
brfss_veterans <- brfss %>%
  filter(veteran == "Yes") %>%
  filter(!is.na(race))

# 2. Count the number of unique entries in the race column for veterans
vet_race_counts <- table(brfss_veterans$race)

# 3. Expected national probabilities (must sum to 1 and match table order)
expected_probs <- c(0.007, 0.061, 0.126, 0.191, 0.024, 0.002, 0.589)

# 4. Run the Chi-Squared Goodness of Fit Test
chisq.test(vet_race_counts, p = expected_probs)


```
```{r} 
# 1. Reshape the data for plotting
plot_data <- final_display %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Expected_Count, Observed_Count), 
    names_to = "Count_Type", 
    values_to = "Count_Value"
  )

# 2. Create the Grouped Bar Plot with Log Scale
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Race, y = Count_Value, fill = Count_Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  # Apply the log transformation
  # 'labels = scales::comma' makes the numbers easier to read (e.g., 1,000 instead of 1e3)
#  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, width = 15)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=14) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs. Expected Veteran Counts by Race (Log Scale)",
    x = "Racial Group",
    y = "Count (Log 10)",
    fill = "Legend"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Expected_Count" = "#2a79d5", "Observed_Count" = "#29b9d6"),
    labels = c("Expected", "Observed")
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank() # Clean up log grid lines
  )
```


```{r}
# Compare veteran race proportions against national expected proportions

observed_counts <- as.numeric(vet_race_counts)
race_names <- names(vet_race_counts)
n_total <- sum(observed_counts)

race_prop_tests <- data.frame(
  Race = race_names,
  Observed_Count = observed_counts,
  Observed_Prop = observed_counts / n_total,
  Expected_Prop = expected_probs
) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    p_value = prop.test(
      x = Observed_Count,
      n = n_total,
      p = Expected_Prop,
      correct = FALSE
    )$p.value
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj_bonferroni = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni"),
    difference = Observed_Prop - Expected_Prop,
    abs_difference = abs(difference)
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

race_prop_tests
```


```{r}
race_prop_tests %>%
  mutate(direction = ifelse(difference > 0, "Overrepresented", "Underrepresented")) %>%
  select(Race, Observed_Prop, Expected_Prop, direction, p_adj_bonferroni)
```

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1. Recreating your processed dataframe based on the screenshot
# (In your actual file, you can just use 'race_prop_tests' from your previous code)
race_prop_tests <- data.frame(
  Race = c("Asian only, non-Hispanic", "Hispanic", "White only, non-Hispanic", 
           "Black only, non-Hispanic", "American Indian or Alaskan Native only, Non-Hispanic",
           "Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander only, Non-Hispanic", "Multiracial, non-Hispanic"),
  Observed_Prop = c(0.012736694, 0.049953993, 0.813162865, 0.074313526, 0.017119473, 0.006344133, 0.026369316),
  Expected_Prop = c(0.061, 0.191, 0.589, 0.126, 0.007, 0.002, 0.024),
  p_adj_bonferroni = c(0, 0, 0, 4.990780e-219, 1.735058e-133, 4.604660e-86, 1.158692e-02)
) %>%
  mutate(direction = ifelse(Observed_Prop > Expected_Prop, "Overrepresented", "Underrepresented"))

# 2. Generate the formatted table
race_prop_tests %>%
  gt() %>%
  # Relabel columns to match your desired style
  cols_label(
    Race = "Race",
    Observed_Prop = "Veteran Prop.",
    Expected_Prop = "National Prop.",
    direction = "Representation",
    p_adj_bonferroni = "p-value (adj)"
  ) %>%
  # Format proportions as decimals (matching your first screenshot style)
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(Observed_Prop, Expected_Prop),
    decimals = 4
  ) %>%
  # Format p-values: small values as < 2.2e-16 or scientific notation
  fmt_scientific(
    columns = p_adj_bonferroni,
    decimals = 2
  ) %>%
  # Apply the "Academic/Minimalist" styling (Thin lines top and bottom)
  tab_options(
    table.border.top.color = "black",
    table.border.top.width = px(2),
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table.border.bottom.width = px(2),
    column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black",
    column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(1),
    table_body.hlines.style = "none", # Removes horizontal lines between rows
    data_row.padding = px(4)
  ) %>%
  # Align text left and numbers right
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = Race
  ) %>%
  # Handle the extremely small p-values to look like the screenshot
  text_transform(
    locations = cells_body(columns = p_adj_bonferroni, rows = p_adj_bonferroni < 2.2e-16),
    fn = function(x) "< 2.2e-16"
  )



```




```{r}

# measuring differences in Demographics: education level

brfss_veterans_edu <- brfss %>%
  filter(veteran == "Yes", age >= 25, !is.na(education))

table(brfss$education, useNA = "ifany")


brfss_veterans_edu <- brfss %>%
  filter(veteran == "Yes", age >= 25, !is.na(education)) %>%
  mutate(edu_group = case_when(
    education %in% c("No school", "Elementary", "Some HS") ~ "Less than high school",
    education == "HS Grad" ~ "High school graduate",
    education == "Some College" ~ "Some college",
    education == "College Grad" ~ "Bachelor's or higher",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(edu_group))
```


```{r}
# Education comparison: BRFSS veterans vs 2022 U.S. national education distribution
## Education comparison: BRFSS veterans vs 2022 U.S. national education distribution
# Source: U.S. Census ACS 2022 S1501, population age 25+

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(readr)

# Census ACS 2022 proportions, age 25+
# These are rounded published values, so we normalize them below.
expected_edu_props <- c(
  "Less than high school" = 0.109,
  "High school graduate" = 0.264,
  "Some college / associate" = 0.285,
  "Bachelor's or higher" = 0.209 + 0.134
)

# Force probabilities to sum exactly to 1
expected_edu_props <- expected_edu_props / sum(expected_edu_props)

# Clean BRFSS veteran education data
brfss_veterans_edu <- brfss %>%
  filter(veteran == "Yes", !is.na(education)) %>%
  mutate(
    age_num = if ("age" %in% names(.)) parse_number(as.character(age)) else NA_real_,
    edu_group = case_when(
      education %in% c("No school", "Elementary", "Some HS") ~ "Less than high school",
      education == "HS Grad" ~ "High school graduate",
      education == "Some College" ~ "Some college / associate",
      education == "College Grad" ~ "Bachelor's or higher",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(edu_group)) %>%
  filter(is.na(age_num) | age_num >= 25)

# Observed counts
observed_edu_counts <- table(brfss_veterans_edu$edu_group)

# Reorder expected probabilities to match observed table
expected_edu_props_ordered <- expected_edu_props[names(observed_edu_counts)]

# Normalize again after reordering, just in case any categories are missing
expected_edu_props_ordered <- expected_edu_props_ordered / sum(expected_edu_props_ordered)

# Chi-square goodness-of-fit test
edu_chisq_test <- chisq.test(
  observed_edu_counts,
  p = expected_edu_props_ordered
)

edu_chisq_test

# Table showing which education groups differ most
edu_diff_table <- data.frame(
  Education = names(observed_edu_counts),
  Observed_Count = as.numeric(observed_edu_counts),
  Expected_Prop = expected_edu_props_ordered
) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = sum(Observed_Count),
    Observed_Prop = Observed_Count / Total,
    Expected_Count = Expected_Prop * Total,
#    Difference = Observed_Prop - Expected_Prop,
#    Percent_Point_Gap = 100 * Difference,
 #   ChiSq_Contribution = (Observed_Count - Expected_Count)^2 / Expected_Count,
    Direction = ifelse(Difference > 0, "Overrepresented", "Underrepresented")
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ChiSq_Contribution))

edu_diff_table

# Education group that differs most
edu_diff_table %>%
  slice_max(ChiSq_Contribution, n = 1)

# Plot observed vs expected proportions
edu_diff_table %>%
  select(Education, Observed_Prop, Expected_Prop) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Observed_Prop, Expected_Prop),
    names_to = "Type",
    values_to = "Proportion"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Education, y = Proportion, fill = Type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Veteran Education Distribution vs 2022 U.S. National Average",
    x = "Education Level",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Group"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
```


```{r}
# One-sample proportion tests for each education group
# with Bonferroni correction

edu_prop_tests <- data.frame(
  Education = names(observed_edu_counts),
  Observed_Count = as.numeric(observed_edu_counts),
  Expected_Prop = expected_edu_props_ordered
) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = sum(Observed_Count),
    Observed_Prop = Observed_Count / Total,
    Difference = Observed_Prop - Expected_Prop,
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    p_value = prop.test(
      x = Observed_Count,
      n = Total,
      p = Expected_Prop,
      correct = FALSE
    )$p.value
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni"),
    Significant_Bonferroni = p_bonferroni < 0.05,
    Direction = ifelse(Difference > 0, "Overrepresented", "Underrepresented")
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_bonferroni)

edu_prop_tests <- edu_prop_tests %>%
  select(
    Education,
    Observed_Prop,
    Expected_Prop,
    p_bonferroni,
    Direction
  )

edu_prop_tests
```




```{r}
# Income comparison: BRFSS veterans vs 2022 U.S. national household income distribution

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# Manually entered 2022 ACS national household income proportions
# Broad categories based on Census ACS B19001
national_income_df <- data.frame(
  Income = c(
    "Less than $25,000",
    "$25,000 to less than $50,000",
    "$50,000 to less than $75,000",
    "$75,000 or more"
  ),
  Expected_Prop = c(
    0.161,
    0.171,
    0.148,
    0.520
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Expected_Prop = Expected_Prop / sum(Expected_Prop))

# Clean BRFSS veteran income data
brfss_veterans_income <- brfss %>%
  filter(veteran == "Yes", !is.na(income)) %>%
  mutate(
    income_chr = as.character(income),
    income_group = case_when(
      income_chr %in% c(
        "Less than $10000",
        "$10000 to $14999",
        "$15000 to $19999",
        "$20000 to $24999"
      ) ~ "Less than $25,000",
      
      income_chr %in% c(
        "$25000 to $34999",
        "$35000 to $49999"
      ) ~ "$25,000 to less than $50,000",
      
      income_chr == "$50000 to $74999" ~ "$50,000 to less than $75,000",
      
      income_chr %in% c(
        "$75000 to $99999",
        "$100000 to $149999",
        "$150000 to $199999",
        "$200000 or more"
      ) ~ "$75,000 or more",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_group))

# Observed veteran income counts
observed_income_counts <- table(brfss_veterans_income$income_group)

# Expected proportions ordered to match observed table
expected_income_props_ordered <- national_income_df$Expected_Prop[
  match(names(observed_income_counts), national_income_df$Income)
]

expected_income_props_ordered <- expected_income_props_ordered / sum(expected_income_props_ordered)

# Chi-square goodness-of-fit test
income_chisq_test <- chisq.test(
  observed_income_counts,
  p = expected_income_props_ordered
)

income_chisq_test

# Table showing which income groups differ most
income_diff_table <- data.frame(
  Income = names(observed_income_counts),
  Observed_Count = as.numeric(observed_income_counts),
  Expected_Prop = expected_income_props_ordered
) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = sum(Observed_Count),
    Observed_Prop = Observed_Count / Total,
    Expected_Count = Expected_Prop * Total,
    Difference = Observed_Prop - Expected_Prop,
    ChiSq_Contribution = (Observed_Count - Expected_Count)^2 / Expected_Count,
    Direction = ifelse(Difference > 0, "Overrepresented", "Underrepresented")
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ChiSq_Contribution))

income_diff_table

# One-sample proportion tests with Bonferroni correction
income_prop_tests <- data.frame(
  Income = names(observed_income_counts),
  Observed_Count = as.numeric(observed_income_counts),
  Expected_Prop = expected_income_props_ordered
) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = sum(Observed_Count),
    Observed_Prop = Observed_Count / Total,
    Difference = Observed_Prop - Expected_Prop
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    p_value = prop.test(
      x = Observed_Count,
      n = Total,
      p = Expected_Prop,
      correct = FALSE
    )$p.value
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni"),
    Direction = ifelse(Difference > 0, "Overrepresented", "Underrepresented")
  ) %>%
  select(
    Income,
    Observed_Prop,
    Expected_Prop,
    p_bonferroni,
    Direction
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_bonferroni)

income_prop_tests
# Plot observed vs expected proportions using same color scheme
income_diff_table %>%
  select(Income, Observed_Prop, Expected_Prop) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Observed_Prop, Expected_Prop),
    names_to = "Type",
    values_to = "Proportion"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Type = recode(
      Type,
      "Observed_Prop" = "Observed",
      "Expected_Prop" = "Expected"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Income, y = Proportion, fill = Type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Expected" = vet_blue, "Observed" = vet_teal)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Veteran Income Distribution vs 2022 U.S. National Average",
    x = "Income Level",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Group"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
```
